23:47.ar: فَقَالُوٓاْ أَنُؤۡمِنُ لِبَشَرَيۡنِ مِثۡلِنَا وَقَوۡمُهُمَا لَنَا عَٰبِدُونَ
23:47.en: And they said: Shall we put faith in two mortals like ourselves, and whose folk are servile unto us

24:11.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُو بِٱلۡإِفۡكِ عُصۡبَةࣱ مِّنكُمۡۚ لَا تَحۡسَبُوهُ شَرࣰّ ا لَّكُمۖ بَلۡ هُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡۚ لِكُلِّ ٱمۡرِيࣲٕ مِّنۡهُم مَّا ٱكۡتَسَبَ مِنَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِۚ وَٱلَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ كِبۡرَهُۥ مِنۡهُمۡ لَهُۥ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
24:11.en: Lo! they who spread the slander are a gang among you. Deem it not a bad thing for you; nay, it is good for you. Unto every man of them (will be paid) that which he hath earned of the sin; and as for him among them who had the greater share therein, his will be an awful doom

24:12.ar: لَّوۡلَآ إِذۡ سَمِعۡتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتُ بِأَنفُسِهِمۡ خَيۡرࣰ ا وَقَالُواْ هَٰذَآ إِفۡكࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
24:12.en: Why did not the believers, men and women, when ye heard it, think good of their own own folk, and say: It is a manifest untruth

24:13.ar: لَّوۡلَا جَآءُو عَلَيۡهِ بِأَرۡبَعَةِ شُهَدَآءَۚ فَإِذۡ لَمۡ يَأۡتُواْ بِٱلشُّهَدَآءِ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُمُ ٱلۡكَٰذِبُونَ
24:13.en: Why did they not produce four witnesses? Since they produce not witnesses, they verily are liars in the sight of Allah

24:14.ar: وَلَوۡلَا فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَرَحۡمَتُهُۥ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ لَمَسَّكُمۡ فِي مَآ أَفَضۡتُمۡ فِيهِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
24:14.en: Had it not been for the grace of Allah and His mercy unto you in the world and the Hereafter an awful doom had overtaken you for that whereof ye murmured

24:15.ar: إِذۡ تَلَقَّوۡنَهُۥ بِأَلۡسِنَتِكُمۡ وَتَقُولُونَ بِأَفۡوَاهِكُم مَّا لَيۡسَ لَكُم بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱ وَتَحۡسَبُونَهُۥ هَيِّنࣰ ا وَهُوَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمࣱ‏
24:15.en: When ye welcomed it with your tongues, and uttered with your mouths that whereof ye had no knowledge, ye counted it a trifle. In the sight of Allah it is very great

24:16.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ إِذۡ سَمِعۡتُمُوهُ قُلۡتُم مَّا يَكُونُ لَنَآ أَن نَّتَكَلَّمَ بِهَٰذَا سُبۡحَٰنَكَ هَٰذَا بُهۡتَٰنٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
24:16.en: Wherefor, when ye heard it, said ye not: It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to Thee (O Allah)! This is awful calumny

24:17.ar: يَعِظُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ أَن تَعُودُواْ لِمِثۡلِهِۦٓ أَبَدًا إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
24:17.en: Allah admonisheth you that ye repeat not the like thereof ever, if ye are (in truth) believers

24:19.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحِبُّونَ أَن تَشِيعَ ٱلۡفَٰحِشَةُ فِي ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمࣱ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
24:19.en: Lo! those who love that slander should be spread concerning those who believe, theirs will be a painful punishment in the world and the Hereafter. Allah knoweth. Ye know not

24:62.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَإِذَا كَانُواْ مَعَهُۥ عَلَىٰٓ أَمۡرࣲ جَامِعࣲ لَّمۡ يَذۡهَبُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَسۡتَـٔۡذِنُوهُۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡتَـٔۡذِنُونَكَ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۚ فَإِذَا ٱسۡتَـٔۡذَنُوكَ لِبَعۡضِ شَأۡنِهِمۡ فَأۡذَن لِّمَن شِئۡتَ مِنۡهُمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمُ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
24:62.en: They only are the true believers who believe in Allah and His messenger and, when they are with him on some common errand, go not away until they have asked leave of him. Lo! those who ask leave of thee, those are they who believe in Allah and His messenger. So, if they ask thy leave for some affair of theirs, give leave to whom thou wilt of them, and ask for them forgiveness of Allah. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

49:12.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱجۡتَنِبُواْ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعۡضَ ٱلظَّنِّ إِثۡمࣱۖ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُواْ وَلَا يَغۡتَب بَّعۡضُكُم بَعۡضًاۚ أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمۡ أَن يَأۡكُلَ لَحۡمَ أَخِيهِ مَيۡتࣰ ا فَكَرِهۡتُمُوهُۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ تَوَّابࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
49:12.en: O ye who believe! Shun much suspicion; for lo! some suspicion is a crime. And spy not, neither backbite one another. Would one of you love to eat the flesh of his dead brother? Ye abhor that (so abhor the other)! And keep your duty (to Allah). Lo! Allah is Relenting, Merciful

43:51.ar: وَنَادَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنُ فِي قَوۡمِهِۦ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَلَيۡسَ لِي مُلۡكُ مِصۡرَ وَهَٰذِهِ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِيٓۚ أَفَلَا تُبۡصِرُونَ
43:51.en: And Pharaoh caused a proclamation to be made among his people saying: O my people! Is not mine the sovereignty of Egypt and these rivers flowing under me? Can ye not then discern

43:52.ar: أَمۡ أَنَا۠ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينࣱ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُبِينُ
43:52.en: I am surely better than this fellow, who is despicable and can hardly make (his meaning) plain

9:80.ar: ٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ أَوۡ لَا تَسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ إِن تَسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ سَبۡعِينَ مَرَّةࣰ فَلَن يَغۡفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَفَرُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
9:80.en: Ask forgiveness for them (O Muhammad), or ask not forgiveness for them; though thou ask forgiveness for them seventy times Allah will not forgive them. That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His messenger, and Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

ef0XEy_1Q8c.speaker: adnan
ef0XEy_1Q8c.speaker_note: Ramadan Quranic Themes series on his channel; speaks as the imam of the centre throughout
ef0XEy_1Q8c.title: Ramadan 2025 Night 17: Correcting Assumptions
ef0XEy_1Q8c.one_line: How the Quran corrects our assumptions about people, through Pharaoh's chiefs, the slander of Aisha, and the companions who asked leave of the Prophet.
ef0XEy_1Q8c.summary: He treats assumptions as a recurring Quranic theme. His teachers held that it is better to make no assumptions at all, and if one must assume, the assumption should be good. Bad assumptions are allowed only where you carry responsibility: in business, when vetting a marriage proposal, and when raising or mentoring someone. He links bad assumptions to a fragile ego and self-worth. From 23:47 he shows Pharaoh's chiefs dismissing Musa because his people were their subjects, and argues that the one who assumes others have nothing to offer is the one who loses; he applies this to workplaces, clinics and a community whose leaders do not listen. From the slander of Aisha in Surah An-Nur he draws that the believers should have thought well 'of themselves', since what we assume of others is a projection of ourselves; he stresses the four-witness standard, the gravity of passing on rumours, the fault of staying silent, and the example of Abu Ayyub and his wife. From 24:62 he teaches giving the benefit of the doubt to those who ask leave or do not show up for community work, while asking each person whether they carry their own weight.

outline.heading: Assumptions as a Quranic theme
outline.gist: Not among the most frequent themes but recurring enough to study: the Quran tells believers to avoid much assumption because some of it is sin.

outline.heading: No assumptions or good assumptions?
outline.gist: Most of his teachers held one should not assume at all without certain knowledge, since a wrong assumption can harm you, the other person and your relationship with Allah.

outline.heading: Exception: business partners
outline.gist: Where money is involved you may suspect the other party and are not blamed for it.

outline.heading: Exception: a suitor for your daughter
outline.gist: Parents may scrutinise a man proposing and search for his faults.

outline.heading: Exception: children and mentees
outline.gist: A parent or mentor must assume the worst to catch mistakes early; a mentee can opt out, a child cannot, and a measured strictness builds character.

outline.heading: The common thread is responsibility
outline.gist: When you are responsible for something you may suspect whoever approaches it; outside that, if you assume, assume good.

outline.heading: Bad assumptions feed a threatened ego
outline.gist: The gym example: when someone threatens what you draw your worth from, you hunt for flaws to feel better; stable self-worth reduces bad assumptions.

outline.heading: Do not reduce a person to a few words
outline.gist: Do not fill in the blanks about people; you would hate having your whole life summed up as 'he is like this'.

outline.heading: Pharaoh's chiefs: nothing good from a subject people
outline.gist: They refused Musa because his people served them, assuming nothing of value could come from them.

outline.heading: Everyone has something to teach you
outline.gist: Assuming someone has nothing to offer is a great lost opportunity; every person, children especially, carries knowledge you lack.

outline.heading: The one who assumes is the one who loses
outline.gist: Musa and his people lost nothing; Pharaoh and his chiefs lost everything by refusing to hear him.

outline.heading: Pharaoh's real reason behind his public narrative
outline.gist: The Quran usually gives Pharaoh's propaganda to his people; here it reveals his own mentality: he would not learn from those he considered inferior.

outline.heading: Ego in the workplace and the clinic
outline.gist: Seniors and physicians who dismiss a junior's fresh perspective miss out; and if you are the junior who is not heard, it is their loss, so keep developing your ideas.

outline.heading: A community whose leaders do not listen
outline.gist: Muslim institutions fail and stay scattered because those in charge assume others know nothing; he blames religious leadership for not listening.

outline.heading: Listening is how an institution grows
outline.gist: He knows little beyond what he teaches; people's complaints show where the problems are, which is why programs are reworked every semester.

outline.heading: The slander of Aisha and how people responded
outline.gist: As the rumour spread people split into those who rejected it, those who stayed silent, those who passed it on, and those who believed it.

outline.heading: Thinking well 'of themselves': assumptions as projection
outline.gist: The verse says believers should have thought well of themselves, because what you assume of others mirrors what you think you would have done.

outline.heading: Assume the best of strangers even against the signs
outline.gist: Even a Muslim staggering with a bottle is given an excuse, unless he is your child, your business partner or a suitor, whom you are responsible to scrutinise.

outline.heading: Four witnesses and others' private lives
outline.gist: An accusation of zina needs four witnesses to a public act; whoever lifts a curtain to see is himself at fault.

outline.heading: What you think trivial is grave to Allah
outline.gist: Passing a rumour from tongue to tongue without knowledge seems small but is enormous to Allah; the right response is to refuse to speak of it.

outline.heading: Never again: fix the cause, switch off the thought
outline.gist: Find why you assume badly and treat it; until then, put away every bad assumption the moment it arises.

outline.heading: Silence is also a fault
outline.gist: Blame fell not only on those who spread the rumour but on those who heard it and said nothing.

outline.heading: Abu Ayyub and his wife
outline.gist: Each asked the other whether they would have done it; neither would, and Aisha and Safwan were better than them, so they rejected it.

outline.heading: Project good assumptions; the harm to the Prophet
outline.gist: Worship Allah by projecting good onto others; the rumour broke the Prophet's heart and made him ill for a month.

outline.heading: Good for you, and those who love indecency to spread
outline.gist: The episode taught the community how to respond next time; those who want evil to spread do so to hide their own, and bad assumptions come from a diseased heart.

outline.heading: Believers ask leave; grant it and seek forgiveness for them
outline.gist: True believers do not leave a collective gathering without permission; the Prophet is told to grant leave and not suspect those who ask.

outline.heading: Community work and 'where is so-and-so?'
outline.gist: Exhausting service tempts workers to suspect those absent; do the work for Allah and do not spend energy assuming bad of others.

outline.heading: His own struggle with this as an imam
outline.gist: He admits he is close to losing patience with a handful doing the work of thousands and has not settled how responsibility fits here.

outline.heading: The Prophet accepting excuses after Tabuk
outline.gist: He accepted every excuse at face value and asked forgiveness for them, leaving the truth to Allah, because the default is good assumption.

outline.heading: Are you carrying your weight?
outline.gist: Turn the question on yourself: when you ask to be excused, is the reason real?

outline.heading: The Prophet noticed everyone: you matter
outline.gist: He asked after each absent companion by name; you matter when you contribute and are accountable when you do not. He closes by restating why to hold good assumptions.

themes.label: Good and bad assumptions about people (husn al-zann)
themes.note: Default to no assumption or a good one; bad assumptions are permitted only where you hold responsibility, and the Quran repeatedly corrects them.

themes.label: Self-value, self-worth, confidence
themes.note: A fragile self-worth drives us to find flaws in anyone who threatens it.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Pharaoh's arrogance stopped him learning from Musa; ego in seniors and physicians makes them ignore juniors.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions
themes.note: Muslim institutions fail because leaders assume others know nothing and do not listen to the community.

themes.label: Guarding the tongue; speech and gossip
themes.note: Spreading or even silently tolerating a rumour about someone's honour is grave before Allah.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: Abu Ayyub and his wife model the right response to slander by judging Aisha by what they themselves would not do.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: Those serving should not suspect absent members, while every individual must carry their share of the work.

themes.label: Parenting and raising children
themes.note: Parents and mentors are responsible to watch for faults, and some strictness builds character.

quran.point: The command to avoid much assumption because some of it is sin
Pharaoh's public boast of ruling Egypt with rivers beneath him and being better than Musa
Asking forgiveness seventy times will not help those who lie, yet the Prophet did not know who was lying and accepted all excuses

hadith.gist: After Tabuk those who stayed behind came one by one with excuses; the Prophet accepted them outwardly, forgave them and asked Allah to forgive them, leaving their inner state to Allah
On campaigns the Prophet would ask about absent companions by name

maxims: If you are going to assume, may it be good
Responsibility is the only licence for bad assumptions
Your assumptions about others project what you think of yourself
The one who assumes is the one who loses
Every person is an opportunity to learn something
You matter when you help and when you don't

stories.who: Pharaoh's chiefs and Musa
stories.point: They dismissed Musa because his people served them, and they, not Musa, were the losers.

stories.who: The slander against Aisha (al-Ifk)
stories.point: Believers should have rejected the rumour outright; spreading it, believing it or staying silent were all failures.

stories.who: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari and Umm Ayyub
stories.point: They reasoned that if they would not commit such a sin, Aisha and Safwan, who were better than them, certainly would not.

stories.who: Those who stayed behind from Tabuk
stories.point: The Prophet accepted their excuses and left their honesty to Allah, modelling good assumption.

Scattered masajid with no collaboration, which he blames on religious leadership that does not listen
Muslim Wellness Network reworks its programs each semester based on community feedback

takeaways: Give anyone you are not responsible for the benefit of the doubt, even when the signs look bad
Work on a stable sense of self-worth so others' success does not push you to look for their faults
Listen to juniors, students, children and community members as people with something to teach you

18:77.ar: فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَتَيَآ أَهۡلَ قَرۡيَةٍ ٱسۡتَطۡعَمَآ أَهۡلَهَا فَأَبَوۡاْ أَن يُضَيِّفُوهُمَا فَوَجَدَا فِيهَا جِدَارࣰ ا يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ فَأَقَامَهُۥۖ قَالَ لَوۡ شِئۡتَ لَتَّخَذۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ أَجۡرࣰ ا
18:77.en: So they twain journeyed on till, when they came unto the folk of a certain township, they asked its folk for food, but they refused to make them guests. And they found therein a wall upon the point of falling into ruin, and he repaired it. (Moses) said: If thou hadst wished, thou couldst have taken payment for it

18:78.ar: قَالَ هَٰذَا فِرَاقُ بَيۡنِي وَبَيۡنِكَۚ سَأُنَبِّئُكَ بِتَأۡوِيلِ مَا لَمۡ تَسۡتَطِع عَّلَيۡهِ صَبۡرًا
18:78.en: He said: This is the parting between thee and me! I will announce unto thee the interpretation of that thou couldst not bear with patience

18:82.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلۡجِدَارُ فَكَانَ لِغُلَٰمَيۡنِ يَتِيمَيۡنِ فِي ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ وَكَانَ تَحۡتَهُۥ كَنزࣱ لَّهُمَا وَكَانَ أَبُوهُمَا صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَأَرَادَ رَبُّكَ أَن يَبۡلُغَآ أَشُدَّهُمَا وَيَسۡتَخۡرِجَا كَنزَهُمَا رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّن رَّبِّكَۚ وَمَا فَعَلۡتُهُۥ عَنۡ أَمۡرِيۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَأۡوِيلُ مَا لَمۡ تَسۡطِع عَّلَيۡهِ صَبۡرࣰ ا
18:82.en: And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was beneath it a treasure belonging to them, and their father had been righteous, and thy Lord intended that they should come to their full strength and should bring forth their treasure as a mercy from their Lord; and I did it not upon my own command. Such is the interpretation of that wherewith thou couldst not bear

19:41.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ صِدِّيقࣰ ا نَّبِيًّا
19:41.en: And make mention (O Muhammad) in the Scripture of Abraham. Lo! he was a saint, a prophet

19:42.ar: إِذۡ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ يَٰٓأَبَتِ لِمَ تَعۡبُدُ مَا لَا يَسۡمَعُ وَلَا يُبۡصِرُ وَلَا يُغۡنِي عَنكَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا
19:42.en: When he said unto his father: O my father! Why worshippest thou that which heareth not nor seeth, nor can in aught avail thee

19:43.ar: يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّي قَدۡ جَآءَنِي مِنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ مَا لَمۡ يَأۡتِكَ فَٱتَّبِعۡنِيٓ أَهۡدِكَ صِرَٰطࣰ ا سَوِيࣰّ ا
19:43.en: O my father! Lo! there hath come unto me of knowledge that which came not unto thee. So follow me, and I will lead thee on a right path

19:44.ar: يَٰٓأَبَتِ لَا تَعۡبُدِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَۖ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ كَانَ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ عَصِيࣰّ ا
19:44.en: O my father! Serve not the devil. Lo! the devil is a rebel unto the Beneficent

19:45.ar: يَٰٓأَبَتِ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ أَن يَمَسَّكَ عَذَابࣱ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ فَتَكُونَ لِلشَّيۡطَٰنِ وَلِيࣰّ ا
19:45.en: O my father! Lo! I fear lest a punishment from the Beneficent overtake thee so that thou become a comrade of the devil

19:46.ar: قَالَ أَرَاغِبٌ أَنتَ عَنۡ ءَالِهَتِي يَٰٓإِبۡرَٰهِيمُۖ لَئِن لَّمۡ تَنتَهِ لَأَرۡجُمَنَّكَۖ وَٱهۡجُرۡنِي مَلِيࣰّ ا
19:46.en: He said: Rejectest thou my gods, O Abraham? If thou cease not, I shall surely stone thee. Depart from me a long while

19:47.ar: قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكَۖ سَأَسۡتَغۡفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّيٓۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ بِي حَفِيࣰّ ا
19:47.en: He said: Peace be unto thee! I shall ask forgiveness of my Lord for thee. Lo! He was ever gracious unto me

19:48.ar: وَأَعۡتَزِلُكُمۡ وَمَا تَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَدۡعُواْ رَبِّي عَسَىٰٓ أَلَّآ أَكُونَ بِدُعَآءِ رَبِّي شَقِيࣰّ ا
19:48.en: I shall withdraw from you and that unto which ye pray beside Allah, and I shall pray unto my Lord. It may be that, in prayer unto my Lord, I shall not be unblest

20:37.en: And indeed, another time, already We have shown thee favour

20:38.ar: إِذۡ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ
20:38.en: When we inspired in thy mother that which is inspired

20:39.ar: أَنِ ٱقۡذِفِيهِ فِي ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقۡذِفِيهِ فِي ٱلۡيَمِّ فَلۡيُلۡقِهِ ٱلۡيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأۡخُذۡهُ عَدُوࣱّ لِّي وَعَدُوࣱّ لَّهُۥۚ وَأَلۡقَيۡتُ عَلَيۡكَ مَحَبَّةࣰ مِّنِّي وَلِتُصۡنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيۡنِيٓ
20:39.en: Saying: Throw him into the ark, and throw it into the river, then the river shall throw it on to the bank, and there an enemy to Me and an enemy to him shall take him. And I endued thee with love from Me that thou mightest be trained according to My will

20:40.ar: إِذۡ تَمۡشِيٓ أُخۡتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكُمۡ عَلَىٰ مَن يَكۡفُلُهُۥۖ فَرَجَعۡنَٰكَ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ كَيۡ تَقَرَّ عَيۡنُهَا وَلَا تَحۡزَنَۚ وَقَتَلۡتَ نَفۡسࣰ ا فَنَجَّيۡنَٰكَ مِنَ ٱلۡغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّٰكَ فُتُونࣰ اۚ فَلَبِثۡتَ سِنِينَ فِيٓ أَهۡلِ مَدۡيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئۡتَ عَلَىٰ قَدَرࣲ يَٰمُوسَىٰ
20:40.en: When thy sister went and said: Shall I show you one who will nurse him? and we restored thee to thy mother that her eyes might be refreshed and might not sorrow. And thou didst kill a man and We delivered thee from great distress, and tried thee with a heavy trial. And thou didst tarry years among the folk of Midian. Then camest thou (hither) by (My) providence, O Moses

9:114.ar: وَمَا كَانَ ٱسۡتِغۡفَارُ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ إِلَّا عَن مَّوۡعِدَةࣲ وَعَدَهَآ إِيَّاهُ فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُۥٓ أَنَّهُۥ عَدُوࣱّ لِّلَّهِ تَبَرَّأَ مِنۡهُۚ إِنَّ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ لَأَوَّٰهٌ حَلِيمࣱ‏
9:114.en: The prayer of Abraham for the forgiveness of his father was only because of a promise he had promised him, but when it had become clear unto him that he (his father) was an enemy to Allah he (Abraham) disowned him. Lo! Abraham was soft of heart, long-suffering

28:10.ar: وَأَصۡبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَٰرِغًاۖ إِن كَادَتۡ لَتُبۡدِي بِهِۦ لَوۡلَآ أَن رَّبَطۡنَا عَلَىٰ قَلۡبِهَا لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
28:10.en: And the heart of the mother of Moses became void, and she would have betrayed him if We had not fortified her heart, that she might be of the believers

500DqeTR15g.title: Ramadan 2025 Night 15: Quranic Themes, Honouring Parents
500DqeTR15g.one_line: Birr al-walidayn rightly understood: not a tool of control, but the barakah of righteous parents, Ibrahim's gentle words to his father, and a mother's love for Musa.
500DqeTR15g.summary: He notes that honouring parents, once a topic everyone nodded along to, now brings red faces, while dishonouring parents is among the signs of the Hour. He warns against using Quranic verses on others when your own interest is involved: read them about yourself, and keep honouring parents after they die by representing them well and caring for siblings, as Yusuf spared his brothers for his parents' sake. Birr does not give parents control over a child's studies, appearance or choice of spouse beyond advising and objecting to real ethical or religious problems; the parent's right is to have their needs met, and overplaying the birr card ruins its sanctity. From 18:82 he explains that Al-Khidr rebuilt the wall to protect two orphans' treasure because their father was righteous, so many unseen blessings in your life may come from your parents' barakah. From 19:41-48 he shows Ibrahim speaking to a hostile father with affection, logic and humility, attributing his insight to knowledge received rather than superiority, and answering threats with peace; children are not tasked with fixing their parents. From 20:37-40 and 28:10 he describes Musa's mother's grief, and ends with the Prophet's answer: your mother, your mother, your mother, then your father.

outline.heading: A famous theme that now stirs emotion
outline.gist: Honouring parents is a hallmark of the faith, and talking about it used to bring easy agreement and sentiment.

outline.heading: From nods to red faces
outline.gist: Over the past decade he has seen disagreement, while some parents ask him to repeat it to their children.

outline.heading: A sign of the Hour
outline.gist: Scholars read the slave woman giving birth to her own master as the mistreatment of parents, among the signs that the Hour is near.

outline.heading: Never use the Quran on others for your own interest
outline.gist: Parents should be careful wielding these verses on their children; read them as commands for yourself, at any age.

outline.heading: Honouring parents after they die
outline.gist: You represent them on earth, and caring for the siblings and family they loved honours them; cutting off a sibling dishonours them.

outline.heading: Yusuf spared his brothers for his parents
outline.gist: He did not punish his brothers partly so his father and mother would not suffer a torn family.

outline.heading: Birr is not control over marriage
outline.gist: Parents may advise on a spouse and push back on real ethical or religious problems, but the choice remains the child's.

outline.heading: The parent's right is support, not your life choices
outline.gist: Culture, income or a course of study are not grounds for invoking birr; the duty is to meet parents' financial, social and emotional needs.

outline.heading: Overplaying the birr card
outline.gist: He often cannot side with parents who demand the ridiculous; overusing a sacred concept, like calling everything haram, empties it of meaning.

outline.heading: The midpoint of Ramadan
outline.gist: The first half welcomes the month and the second bids it farewell, so cherish this last night of welcoming it.

outline.heading: Al-Khidr as a symbol of Allah's decree
outline.gist: His actions represent knowledge we cannot learn from or imitate, such as why a child's life is taken.

outline.heading: The stingy village and the wall
outline.gist: Refused food and water, Al-Khidr rebuilt their collapsing wall for free, and Musa objected.

outline.heading: Decree cannot always be reasoned out
outline.gist: Musa tried to understand logically, so they parted; some say he witnessed more incidents but objected only three times.

outline.heading: The wall belonged to two orphans
outline.gist: A treasure lay beneath it, their father was righteous, and Allah wanted them to grow up and take it themselves; none of it was his own decision.

outline.heading: Why rebuilding protected the treasure
outline.gist: Had the wall fallen soon, the village's untrustworthy people would have controlled the young orphans' wealth.

outline.heading: We know almost nothing
outline.gist: Our sliver of knowledge cannot show what is best; we plan, do our best and trust the One who knows all.

outline.heading: The barakah of righteous parents
outline.gist: Allah's command to honour parents reflects that you live through the barakah of their hard work.

outline.heading: Even parents who are not Muslim
outline.gist: Many companions had non-Muslim parents, yet the good their parents did could still benefit them, unearned.

outline.heading: Why the father is mentioned
outline.gist: The verse would make sense without the phrase, but Allah names the reason: you do not know what good reached you, or what harm was held back, because of your parents.

outline.heading: The boys never knew
outline.gist: They likely found the treasure and lived well without knowing it was their father's goodness, as we often do.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's longest talk with his father
outline.gist: The most detailed account of their conversation; Ibrahim was heartbroken that his father would not join him and instead cursed and threatened him.

outline.heading: Ya abati: the language of affection
outline.gist: Ibrahim used an endearing form of 'my father' to soften his heart, the kind of pet name children use with parents.

outline.heading: A logical question and knowledge received
outline.gist: He asked why worship what neither hears nor sees, then said it was not his father's fault, he had simply received knowledge.

outline.heading: Do not follow Shaytan; I fear for you
outline.gist: He warned against following one who does not love him, used the name Ar-Rahman, and voiced fear for his father.

outline.heading: It is not your job to fix your parents
outline.gist: Parents rarely change because their children tell them to; your role is to honour, help and protect them.

outline.heading: Only knowledge tips the scales
outline.gist: Ibrahim spoke because revelation gave him something his father lacked; if you truly outlearn your parents it will show in how you live.

outline.heading: The arrogance of lecturing parents
outline.gist: Objecting because your culture differs from theirs, or claiming to have figured it all out, lacks adab; Ibrahim asked, explained, showed care and expressed fear.

outline.heading: His father's threat
outline.gist: His father threatened to stone him and disowned him.

outline.heading: Peace be upon you
outline.gist: Ibrahim answered with peace and a promise to ask forgiveness for him, which he was later told to stop.

outline.heading: Respect for a father who opposed him
outline.gist: Though his father helped throw him into the fire, Ibrahim stayed respectful, as the Prophet pleaded with Abu Talib; losing a loved one outside Islam is a unique pain.

outline.heading: Musa's fear before Pharaoh
outline.gist: When Musa grew anxious about his mission, Allah reminded him of what He revealed to his mother.

outline.heading: Casting her baby into the Nile
outline.gist: A mother placed her child in a chest on the river toward an enemy; Allah cast His love on Musa so he would be raised under His eye.

outline.heading: His sister and the return to his mother
outline.gist: His sister offered Pharaoh's household a nurse, and Musa was returned so his mother's eye would be cooled.

outline.heading: Her heart became empty
outline.gist: Narrations describe her staring into nothing, unable to hear, see or eat, such is a parent's love.

outline.heading: You understand your parents once you are one
outline.gist: Raising your own child shows how hard it is to hold a family together, and changes how you see your parents.

outline.heading: Your mother, your mother, your mother
outline.gist: They gave you their best years, so you owe them some of yours, not weeks without care while you are strong.

37:99.ar: وَقَالَ إِنِّي ذَاهِبٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّي سَيَهۡدِينِ
37:99.en: And he said: Lo! I am going unto my Lord Who will guide me

37:100.en: My Lord! Vouchsafe me of the righteous

37:101.en: So We gave him tidings of a gentle son

37:102.ar: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعۡيَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَيَّ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰ فِي ٱلۡمَنَامِ أَنِّيٓ أَذۡبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرۡ مَاذَا تَرَىٰۚ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفۡعَلۡ مَا تُؤۡمَرُۖ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
37:102.en: And when (his son) was old enough to walk with him, (Abraham) said: O my dear son, I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice thee. So look, what thinkest thou? He said: O my father! Do that which thou art commanded. Allah willing, thou shalt find me of the steadfast

37:103.en: Then, when they had both surrendered (to Allah), and he had flung him down upon his face

37:104.en: We called unto him: O Abraham

37:105.ar: قَدۡ صَدَّقۡتَ ٱلرُّءۡيَآۚ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
37:105.en: Thou hast already fulfilled the vision. Lo! thus do We reward the good

37:106.en: Lo! that verily was a clear test

37:107.en: Then We ransomed him with a tremendous victim

37:108.en: And We left for him among the later folk (the salutation)

37:110.en: Thus do We reward the good

37:111.en: Lo! he is one of Our believing slaves

37:112.ar: وَبَشَّرۡنَٰهُ بِإِسۡحَٰقَ نَبِيࣰّ ا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
37:112.en: And we gave him tidings of the birth of Isaac, a prophet of the righteous

37:113.ar: وَبَٰرَكۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ وَعَلَىٰٓ إِسۡحَٰقَۚ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحۡسِنࣱ وَظَالِمࣱ لِّنَفۡسِهِۦ مُبِينࣱ‏
37:113.en: And We blessed him and Isaac. And of their seed are some who do good, and some who plainly wrong themselves

25:74.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبۡ لَنَا مِنۡ أَزۡوَٰجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّٰتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعۡيُنࣲ وَٱجۡعَلۡنَا لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا
25:74.en: And who say: Our Lord! Vouchsafe us comfort of our wives and of our offspring, and make us patterns for (all) those who ward off (evil)

11:72.ar: قَالَتۡ يَٰوَيۡلَتَىٰٓ ءَأَلِدُ وَأَنَا۠ عَجُوزࣱ وَهَٰذَا بَعۡلِي شَيۡخًاۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَشَيۡءٌ عَجِيبࣱ‏
11:72.en: She said: Oh woe is me! Shall I bear a child when I am an old woman, and this my husband is an old man? Lo! this is a strange thing

14:37.ar: رَّبَّنَآ إِنِّيٓ أَسۡكَنتُ مِن ذُرِّيَّتِي بِوَادٍ غَيۡرِ ذِي زَرۡعٍ عِندَ بَيۡتِكَ ٱلۡمُحَرَّمِ رَبَّنَا لِيُقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ فَٱجۡعَلۡ أَفۡـِٔدَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهۡوِيٓ إِلَيۡهِمۡ وَٱرۡزُقۡهُم مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَشۡكُرُونَ
14:37.en: Our Lord! Lo! I have settled some of my posterity in an uncultivable valley near unto Thy holy House, our Lord! that they may establish proper worship; so incline some hearts of men that they may yearn toward them, and provide Thou them with fruits in order that they may be thankful

22:37.ar: لَن يَنَالَ ٱللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلَا دِمَآؤُهَا وَلَٰكِن يَنَالُهُ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ مِنكُمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ سَخَّرَهَا لَكُمۡ لِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
22:37.en: Their flesh and their food reach not Allah, but the devotion from you reacheth Him. Thus have We made them subject unto you that ye may magnify Allah that He hath guided you. And give good tidings (O Muhammad) to the good

4:66.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّا كَتَبۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَنِ ٱقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ أَوِ ٱخۡرُجُواْ مِن دِيَٰرِكُم مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡۖ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ فَعَلُواْ مَا يُوعَظُونَ بِهِۦ لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ وَأَشَدَّ تَثۡبِيتࣰ ا
4:66.en: And if We had decreed for them: Lay down your lives or go forth from your dwellings, but few of them would have done it; though if they did what they are exhorted to do it would be better for them, and more strengthening

22:78.ar: وَجَٰهِدُواْ فِي ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِۦۚ هُوَ ٱجۡتَبَىٰكُمۡ وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنۡ حَرَجࣲۚ مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمۡ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَۚ هُوَ سَمَّىٰكُمُ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ مِن قَبۡلُ وَفِي هَٰذَا لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِۚ فَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱعۡتَصِمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ هُوَ مَوۡلَىٰكُمۡۖ فَنِعۡمَ ٱلۡمَوۡلَىٰ وَنِعۡمَ ٱلنَّصِيرُ
22:78.en: And strive for Allah with the endeavour which is His right. He hath chosen you and hath not laid upon you in religion any hardship; the faith of your father Abraham (is yours). He hath named you Muslims of old time and in this (Scripture), that the messenger may be a witness against you, and that ye may be witnesses against mankind. So establish worship, pay the poor-due, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protecting friend. A blessed Patron and a blessed Helper

cGLO0v5OaDc.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Saffat, Part 6: Verses 99-113
cGLO0v5OaDc.one_line: Ibrahim's sacrifice of his son as the surah's centrepiece: forty years awaiting a dua, a command he never questioned, and why Allah never commands harm.
cGLO0v5OaDc.summary: He calls the sacrifice the main story of the surah, relived every year in Hajj, and explains that the Quran retells stories from different angles, detailing in each surah the part that serves its theme. After the fire, Ibrahim emigrates from his native land and asks for a righteous child, the dua every parent should make, since a child who strays is a lasting heartbreak. Some forty years pass between that dua and the good news of a forbearing son, so we should not be impatient or forget the duas we made. He recounts Hajar and Ismail left beside the Kaaba, which predates Ibrahim, the spring of Zamzam and the Jurhum who settled there, and argues that all of Ibrahim's descendants, Arabs included, are Hebrews, so expelling Palestinians to make room for 'the Hebrews' is absurd. When the son came of age, Ibrahim saw the same vision three nights in a row. The Quran's great arguer and critical thinker raised no objection here, and Ismail answered that his father should do as commanded. That is the meaning of aslama, full submission, though one must first be certain that something truly is Allah's command. They rejected Shaytan at the places now marked by the jamarat, the blade struck without cutting, and a ram ransomed the boy. Because the act had no benefit, it never happened: Allah tests submission but never commands harm, which Eid celebrates.

outline.heading: Opening
The main story of the surah, relived in Hajj
outline.gist: Most of Hajj traces Ibrahim's steps in this story, in which he receives an unthinkable command.

outline.heading: Each surah tells the part of the story it needs
outline.gist: Nuh's defence is detailed in one surah and the ship and his son in Hud; this is the only place the sacrifice is told.

outline.heading: Subtle differences are purposeful
outline.gist: Noticing what is added or left out across retellings reveals what Allah wants us to focus on.

outline.heading: 'I am going to my Lord': emigrating from Babylon
outline.gist: Saved from the fire, Ibrahim had to leave Babylon because he was no longer welcome.

outline.heading: The dua for a righteous child
outline.gist: Every parent's dua, because a child who goes their own way is a heartbreak one never gets over.

outline.heading: Forty years between two verses
outline.gist: Thirty seconds of recitation spans four decades; humans want answers now, but a forbearing son came to a patient father.

outline.heading: Sarah, Hajar and the order of the sons
outline.gist: Sarah bore Ishaq only in old age; Ismail came from Hajar, met in Egypt, after travels through Sham and Palestine.

outline.heading: Do not let time make you forget your dua
outline.gist: The answer may come decades later, and the son granted reflected the patience Ibrahim showed.

outline.heading: Hajar and Ismail in the barren valley
outline.gist: Ibrahim left them where the Kaaba stood, a house that predates him and even Adam, saddened by how barren it was.

outline.heading: Zamzam and the Jurhum
outline.gist: The spring sustained Hajar, and a displaced Yemeni tribe asked her permission and paid to settle beside it; Ismail grew up and married among them.

outline.heading: All Ibrahim's descendants are Hebrews
outline.gist: Arabs through Ismail and Jews through Ishaq both descend from Ibrahim, so removing Palestinians to make room for 'the Hebrews' makes no sense.

outline.heading: When the son reached the age of working with him
outline.gist: The age when a son becomes helpful and a father is proudest of him.

outline.heading: The vision repeated three nights
outline.gist: Ibrahim hoped the first dream was from Shaytan; by the third night he knew it was revelation to slaughter his only, long-awaited son.

outline.heading: The great arguer does not argue
outline.gist: The Quran's example of critical thinking asks not one question here, because he knew this command was not debatable.

outline.heading: 'Do as you are commanded': both submit
outline.gist: Aslama means full submission of will; Ismail, raised to understand prophecy, tells his father he will be patient.

outline.heading: First be certain it is Allah's command
outline.gist: Ibrahim waited three nights; we must verify through proper learning and scholars, not hearsay, then submit fully.

outline.heading: Shaytan at the jamarat
outline.gist: Shaytan tried to make father, son and mother question the command, and each drove him off with pebbles, as pilgrims do today.

outline.heading: Face down, and the knife struck
outline.gist: Ismail asked to be turned face down; Ibrahim, practised at slaughter, truly struck with a sharpened blade.

outline.heading: You have fulfilled the vision: the clear trial
outline.gist: The blade left no mark; Allah called out that he had fulfilled the vision, the reward of excellence, and that this was the manifest trial.

outline.heading: Ransomed because there was no benefit in it
outline.gist: A ram was sent; the killing had no wisdom, so it did not happen, and Allah never commanded anything harmful.

outline.heading: Submission only when you understand is not submission
outline.gist: We cannot understand everything; Eid celebrates that we were never asked to do anything without benefit.

outline.heading: Ibrahim, the epitome of submission
outline.gist: He named us Muslims because he submitted his will without knowing the wisdom; Allah has no need for a child's blood.

outline.heading: Peace upon Ibrahim, and Ishaq fifty years later
outline.gist: His good name endures, and the good news of Ishaq came decades after, with both righteous and oppressive descendants.

25:27.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يَعَضُّ ٱلظَّالِمُ عَلَىٰ يَدَيۡهِ يَقُولُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي ٱتَّخَذۡتُ مَعَ ٱلرَّسُولِ سَبِيلࣰ ا
25:27.en: On the day when the wrong-doer gnaweth his hands, he will say: Ah, would that I had chosen a way together with the messenger (of Allah)

25:28.ar: يَٰوَيۡلَتَىٰ لَيۡتَنِي لَمۡ أَتَّخِذۡ فُلَانًا خَلِيلࣰ ا
25:28.en: Alas for me! Ah, would that I had never taken such an one for friend

25:29.ar: لَّقَدۡ أَضَلَّنِي عَنِ ٱلذِّكۡرِ بَعۡدَ إِذۡ جَآءَنِيۗ وَكَانَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ خَذُولࣰ ا
25:29.en: He verily led me astray from the Reminder after it had reached me. Satan was ever man's deserter in the hour of need

26:90.en: And the Garden will be brought nigh for those who ward off (evil)

26:92.en: And it will be said unto them: Where is (all) that ye used to worship

26:93.en: Instead of Allah? Can they help you or help themselves

26:94.en: Then will they be hurled therein, they and the seducers

26:95.en: And the hosts of Iblis, together

26:96.en: And they will say, when they are quarrelling therein

26:97.ar: تَٱللَّهِ إِن كُنَّا لَفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينٍ
26:97.en: By Allah, of a truth we were in error manifest

26:98.en: When we made you equal with the Lord of the Worlds

26:99.en: It was but the guilty who misled us

26:102.ar: فَلَوۡ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةࣰ فَنَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
26:102.en: Oh, that we had another turn (on earth), that we might be of the believers

27:17.ar: وَحُشِرَ لِسُلَيۡمَٰنَ جُنُودُهُۥ مِنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ وَٱلۡإِنسِ وَٱلطَّيۡرِ فَهُمۡ يُوزَعُونَ
27:17.en: And there were gathered together unto Solomon his armies of the jinn and humankind, and of the birds, and they were set in battle order

27:18.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَتَوۡاْ عَلَىٰ وَادِ ٱلنَّمۡلِ قَالَتۡ نَمۡلَةࣱ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّمۡلُ ٱدۡخُلُواْ مَسَٰكِنَكُمۡ لَا يَحۡطِمَنَّكُمۡ سُلَيۡمَٰنُ وَجُنُودُهُۥ وَهُمۡ لَا يَشۡعُرُونَ
27:18.en: Till, when they reached the Valley of the Ants, an ant exclaimed: O ants! Enter your dwellings lest Solomon and his armies crush you, unperceiving

27:19.ar: فَتَبَسَّمَ ضَاحِكࣰ ا مِّن قَوۡلِهَا وَقَالَ رَبِّ أَوۡزِعۡنِيٓ أَنۡ أَشۡكُرَ نِعۡمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَيَّ وَأَنۡ أَعۡمَلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا تَرۡضَىٰهُ وَأَدۡخِلۡنِي بِرَحۡمَتِكَ فِي عِبَادِكَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
27:19.en: And (Solomon) smiled, laughing at her speech, and said: My Lord, arouse me to be thankful for Thy favour wherewith Thou hast favoured me and my parents, and to do good that shall be pleasing unto Thee, and include me in (the number of) Thy righteous slaves

27:20.ar: وَتَفَقَّدَ ٱلطَّيۡرَ فَقَالَ مَالِيَ لَآ أَرَى ٱلۡهُدۡهُدَ أَمۡ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡغَآئِبِينَ
27:20.en: And he sought among the birds and said: How is it that I see not the hoopoe, or is he among the absent

JCh1gpy2pAE.title: Ramadan 2025 Night 18: Companionship
JCh1gpy2pAE.one_line: The Quran on companionship: the regret of one led astray by a friend, the people of the Fire with no intimate friend, and Sulayman's ant and hoopoe.
JCh1gpy2pAE.summary: He presents companionship as a universal truth: whatever you aim for, the people around you decide whether you get there. The Prophet called his followers companions rather than followers, and since time is the one capital that only decreases, you must be selective about who receives it, at every age and even more so as you get older and set in your ways. From 25:27-29 he describes the wrongdoer biting his hands in regret that can no longer be fixed, and tells the story of Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, who softened toward Islam while his best friend was away and then turned back at his friend's demand. He advises demoting harmful friends to a more distant circle rather than making them enemies. From 26:90-102 he draws that the people of the Fire have no intimate friend left outside to speak for them, that a bad friend acts as one of Iblis's soldiers, and that no one reaches Paradise or Hell alone. From 27:17-20 he reads the ant warning her community and Sulayman missing the hoopoe as signs that good companionship exists even among animals. He urges people to shed dead weight and attach their hearts to the right people, since a person is gathered with those he loves.

outline.heading: Companionship as a timeless concern
outline.gist: Every tradition stresses it because humans do not function without good company; bad company can ruin a life, and sometimes being alone is better than either.

outline.heading: Why the Prophet called them companions
outline.gist: He used 'ashab', not followers, signalling a group of friends working together and benefiting from each other rather than a leader with subordinates.

outline.heading: Time is the capital you can never recover
outline.gist: We are selective about money, holidays and clothes but should be most selective about who gets our hours.

outline.heading: Admitting a friendship was a waste
outline.gist: Looking back in your thirties or forties you may see friendships that gave nothing; be honest about whether the investment was worth it.

outline.heading: Companionship matters more as you age
outline.gist: Children change friends constantly, but older people grow set in their ways, so a poor circle is harder to escape; people in their forties and fifties whose friends are elsewhere feel foreign in the masjid.

outline.heading: Parents who drop their children at the masjid
outline.gist: Children learn by watching; he admires fathers who sit through lessons they do not need so that their children will.

outline.heading: You follow the religion of your best friend
outline.gist: You become like your closest friend; a like-minded friend who reminds you, lifts you and holds you accountable is a rare treasure.

outline.heading: The wrongdoer biting his hands
outline.gist: An Arabic expression for the deepest remorse, perhaps a form of punishing oneself.

outline.heading: Regret that can no longer be fixed
outline.gist: In this life you can still repent; on the Day of Judgment the outcome is fixed and regret peaks.

outline.heading: 'I wish I had not taken so-and-so as a friend'
outline.gist: The generic 'fulan' lets every reader apply it; the friend led him away from the reminder after it reached him.

outline.heading: Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt softens toward Islam
outline.gist: A fierce abuser of the Prophet began listening and stopped his harm while his best friend was away on a caravan.

outline.heading: His friend's ultimatum and the end at Badr
outline.gist: On returning, his friend refused to speak to him until he spat in the Prophet's face; he chose his friend and died beside him.

outline.heading: Shaytan always deserts you
outline.gist: The bad friend's influence feels like loyalty but pulls the heart away from Allah.

outline.heading: Circles of friendship: demote, do not make enemies
outline.gist: Move a harmful best friend to a more distant circle by being less available; explain if needed. This is an obligation, not an option.

outline.heading: Bad company cost him the Prophet's companionship
outline.gist: He could have been a sahabi but chose to be the companion of an enemy of the Prophet; choose who influences you before it is too late.

outline.heading: Paradise brought near; 'where are those you worshipped?'
outline.gist: Paradise is brought close to the mindful and Hell exposed to the lost, who are asked whether their false priorities can help them.

outline.heading: Thrown in together with the soldiers of Iblis
outline.gist: The doubled verb pictures them tipped in one after another, and the mention of Iblis's soldiers prepares what follows.

outline.heading: Quarrelling in the Fire
outline.gist: They admit they were lost when they equated others with the Lord of the worlds and blame the criminals who misled them.

outline.heading: No intercessor and no intimate friend
outline.gist: Everyone who cared about them is in the Fire with them; a single friend on the right side might have spoken for them.

outline.heading: A bad friend is a soldier of Iblis
outline.gist: We all know right from wrong; the bad friend makes the haram look normal and walks you several steps toward it.

outline.heading: Shaytan works through the person he has won
outline.gist: His whisper is weak and fades with a good deed, so he sends one fully indulging person into others' lives to infect them.

outline.heading: No one reaches Paradise or Hell alone
outline.gist: People are gathered in groups; except for a prophet whom no one followed, walking alone is not an option, and you go where your friends go.

outline.heading: Finding good friends is an obligation at any age
outline.gist: Without company that strengthens your iman you will not make it; distance yourself from those who do not help and find those who will.

outline.heading: Sulayman's army of jinn, men and birds
outline.gist: His sovereignty included soldiers of every kind gathered for him as they marched through a valley of ants.

outline.heading: The ant warns her community: why Sulayman smiled
outline.gist: He realised good companionship exists even among insects: someone who looks out for you and warns of danger.

outline.heading: Sulayman's gratitude for his companions
outline.gist: Danger is not always evil intent, yet you still need someone to warn you; Sulayman asks Allah to help him thank Him for the blessing of those around him.

outline.heading: 'Where is the hoopoe?' An animal as a better companion
outline.gist: The hoopoe's scouting brought Sulayman knowledge he could not have gained otherwise; some animals serve you better than some people.

outline.heading: Shed the dead weight
outline.gist: Here you must put yourself first: help those you can, but when someone only takes you away from Allah, remove them sooner rather than later.

outline.heading: Gathered with those your heart loved
outline.gist: On the Day of Judgment a person is with the people he loved, so attach your heart to the right group now, especially before age sets you in your ways.

49:14.ar: ۞قَالَتِ ٱلۡأَعۡرَابُ ءَامَنَّاۖ قُل لَّمۡ تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَلَٰكِن قُولُوٓاْ أَسۡلَمۡنَا وَلَمَّا يَدۡخُلِ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۖ وَإِن تُطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ لَا يَلِتۡكُم مِّنۡ أَعۡمَٰلِكُمۡ شَيۡـًٔاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
49:14.en: The wandering Arabs say: We believe. Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Ye believe not, but rather say "We submit," for the faith hath not yet entered into your hearts. Yet, if ye obey Allah and His messenger, He will not withhold from you aught of (the reward of) your deeds. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

90:11.en: But he hath not attempted the Ascent

90:12.en: Ah, what will convey unto thee what the Ascent is

MV-eErTg80k.title: Tazkiyah Pearls 9: Values and Tawbah
MV-eErTg80k.one_line: Why habitual sin reveals what we truly believe, how principles become values, and why real tawbah needs genuine remorse and a plan.
MV-eErTg80k.summary: He first closes the topic of humbleness: it is simply recognising our reality as servants, so self-proclaimed or artificial humility is a form of arrogance, and without humbleness nobody can learn. He then lays out four levels: a principle from the Quran makes a value valid, a value is the deep definition you carry, an ethic is how it shows up in a given situation, and behaviour is the lifelong practice. The core problem is the gap between what we say we believe and what we actually believe. Using lowering the gaze as an example for men, he argues that a sin repeated constantly is not weakness but a hidden belief that it is not really wrong, buried in an inner black box nobody wants to open. Some go further and bend the religion to match their habits. Values must be consistent, not conditional, which is the steep path of the Quran. Tazkiyah, technically, is turning Quranic principles into values. He then teaches tawbah as the clearest window into values: it needs remorse, stopping now, and a plan. Remorse is impossible if you never believed the act was wrong, and nostalgia for past sins shows tawbah has not happened. A plan removes the cause each time, so tawbah from one sin gradually cleans out many. He ends by urging deep reflection to define values with their real exceptions.

outline.heading: Humbleness is the servant's reality; artificial humility is arrogance
outline.gist: Allah's essence is greatness; ours is servitude, so humbleness is just honesty about what we are. Declaring your own humility reveals arrogance.

outline.heading: Seeking strength and status through Allah
outline.gist: Wanting integrity and status is fine, but they must be sought from Allah who owns them and grants them lastingly.

outline.heading: Be the humble company you enjoy
outline.gist: Humble people are easy to be around because they do not compare or point out flaws; become that person.

outline.heading: Without humbleness you cannot learn
outline.gist: Learning requires admitting ignorance; the humble learn from anyone, of any age or background, and learn fastest.

outline.heading: Serve even before you understand
outline.gist: Service manifests humbleness and can make up for a lack of clarity on the concepts.

outline.heading: Principle, value, ethic and behaviour
outline.gist: The principle validates a value; the value is honesty defined in depth; using honesty as the example.

outline.heading: Ethics shift with the situation; the Quran supplies principles
outline.gist: The definition of honesty stays fixed while its expression changes by question and setting; principles are already set by the Quran.

outline.heading: What you claim to believe versus what you really believe
outline.gist: Beliefs float in the psyche as nice ideas until they are captured and made second nature, which takes time.

outline.heading: The bedouins told to say 'we submitted'
outline.gist: Allah corrected their claim of full faith, showing a transitional period before belief enters the heart.

outline.heading: Lowering the gaze: habitual sin is not weakness
outline.gist: Everyone says looking is forbidden, yet most do it constantly; frequent sin shows a gap between claimed and real belief.

outline.heading: The black box of real values
outline.gist: Most never open the sealed box inside; doing so reveals a long scroll of excuses that is the true belief.

outline.heading: Bending the religion to fit our habits
outline.gist: Some, rather than change, reinterpret Allah's words to match their values, producing a morphed Islam rooted in arrogance and fear of change.

outline.heading: Values are consistent, not conditional
outline.gist: Generosity only when wealthy or in a good mood is a preference, not a value.

outline.heading: The steep path: giving when you are also in need
outline.gist: Freeing a slave or feeding the hungry on a day of hunger is the obstacle that proves an ethic is unconditional.

outline.heading: Tazkiyah defined: turning Quranic principles into values
outline.gist: Once values are correctly coded, ongoing coaching is unnecessary; failure to practise usually means you do not really accept the ruling.

outline.heading: Do we truly believe in accountability?
outline.gist: Extended to resurrection and judgment, the same gap explains the state of the ummah; facing real beliefs is frightening but the first step.

outline.heading: Tawbah: the door that never closes
outline.gist: The Prophet repented a hundred times a day; the door stays open until the sun rises from the west or death arrives.

outline.heading: The elements of tawbah
outline.gist: Remorse for the past, stopping the sin now, and a plan for the future, plus restitution where rights were taken.

outline.heading: Remorse requires believing the act was wrong
outline.gist: Regret is the core of tawbah, and you cannot regret what you never thought was wrong.

outline.heading: Outgrowing a sin or missing it is not tawbah
outline.gist: Stopping because of age, sickness or lack of time, or looking back fondly on those days, means tawbah has not happened.

outline.heading: Using Allah's principles to feel superior
outline.gist: Saying a lifestyle is forbidden because it feels good to say, while craving it inside, is another kind of arrogance.

outline.heading: Why men fall: an unconvinced value meets opportunity
outline.gist: Craving the forbidden comes from not being convinced it should be forbidden; when power and status arrive later in life, the hidden belief surfaces.

outline.heading: Expose your values before time exposes them
outline.gist: Allah conceals your true beliefs; it is your job to uncover and change them, reaching genuine regret.

outline.heading: The plan: find and remove the culprit
outline.gist: Ask why you sinned: a value, environment, friends, timing, routine. Intention alone with nothing changed guarantees a relapse.

outline.heading: Tawbah from one sin becomes tawbah from all
outline.gist: Each relapse reveals another cause to remove; since sins feed one another, clearing influences removes sins you no longer notice.

outline.heading: Building a value through reflection
outline.gist: Contemplate a value like honesty in depth, knowing its genuine exceptions so you do not invent new ones.

JfRfr6X77Mg.title: Ramadan 2025 Night 16: Quranic Themes, Your Relationship with Allah
JfRfr6X77Mg.one_line: The unique relationship with Allah: dhikr that brings contentment (20:130), Yunus owning his mistake in the whale (21:87-88), and reverence for Allah's rituals (22:32).
JfRfr6X77Mg.summary: He separates three Quranic themes: knowing Allah, which grounds faith; obeying Allah, which rests on the difference in status between Creator and creation; and the relationship with Allah, a lifelong path with no limit to how close one can come, and the true theme of Ramadan. No other relationship resembles it, since Allah is unseen and does not reply in words, and we struggle even with human relationships. Yet research such as the long Harvard study shows relationships are what bring people fulfilment, and this one brings the most; in Ramadan Allah opens the door for a fresh start. From 20:130 he explains that the Prophet, whose plan to win Makkah did not unfold as hoped, was told to persevere and glorify his Lord at every hour so that he would be content: dhikr gains Allah nothing and gives us everything. From 21:87-88 he retells Yunus leaving his people in anger without permission, the three lots, and his words in the whale's belly, an apology that fully owns the mistake, which Allah promises to answer for every believer in their own darkness. From 22:32 he teaches that revering Allah's rituals and commands is the sign of taqwa in the heart.

outline.heading: Knowing, obeying and relating to Allah
outline.gist: Knowing Allah comes before belief; obedience rests on the gap between the finite servant and the infinite Lord; the relationship is a third, separate theme.

outline.heading: A top Quranic theme
outline.gist: Whole passages and surahs describe what to aim for, avoid and repair in the relationship with Allah.

outline.heading: A lifelong path and the theme of Ramadan
outline.gist: There is no end to how close or how far one can be, and mending this relationship is what Ramadan is for.

outline.heading: No other relationship is like it
outline.gist: He is unseen and does not answer in words; we barely manage relationships we practise daily, so this one needs sensitivity to how He responds.

outline.heading: The most beautiful relationship of all
outline.gist: Parents, spouse, children and friends bring deep fulfilment, but this relationship, built well, surpasses them.

outline.heading: What brings people happiness
outline.gist: A 75-year Harvard study found that beyond basic needs, meaningful relationships, not money or fame, gave people satisfaction and longer lives.

outline.heading: Ramadan's open door
outline.gist: The most fulfilling relationship is with Allah, who in Ramadan offers a new page as if you had never sinned, because He created you for this.

outline.heading: The finite connecting with the Infinite
outline.gist: A mortal finding connection with the Divine, beyond time and space, is what makes life worthwhile, and ignoring it is a tragedy.

outline.heading: Be patient with what they say
outline.gist: Facing rejection and mockery, the Prophet was told to persevere, since guidance cannot be forced on those you love.

outline.heading: Plans that did not work out
outline.gist: He planned to win Quraysh's leaders, then Makkah, then the Arabs, and it did not happen; plans rarely go as hoped, so adapt.

outline.heading: Glorify your Lord at every hour
outline.gist: Before sunrise, before sunset, in the night and at the ends of the day: engage in praise at every moment you find.

outline.heading: So that you may be content
outline.gist: Praising Allah adds nothing to Him; the result is a calm and satisfaction you could not find any other way.

outline.heading: All the benefit is ours
outline.gist: The relationship is built on what is in it for us: contentment instead of always chasing the next thing, which is why we come every night.

outline.heading: Dhun-Nun storms out in anger
outline.gist: Yunus was angry at his people, not at Allah, for refusing to listen after three days' warning, and left the city.

outline.heading: A prophet may not leave without permission
outline.gist: He thought he would not be held to account because he acted out of love, and he was wrong.

outline.heading: His people were destined to repent
outline.gist: Within those three days his people were to repent and be forgiven, and by leaving he left them no one to turn to.

outline.heading: Three straws
outline.gist: On an overloaded ship they drew lots to throw someone overboard, and his name came up three times, so he understood the message.

outline.heading: A noble feeling, a wrong assessment
outline.gist: His grief for his people looks noble, but Allah's terms with His prophets are clear; he went overboard and was swallowed.

outline.heading: Ashamed in the belly of the whale
outline.gist: Distressed and ashamed, he had the self-accountability to admit the decision was never his to make, and saw his plight as mercy.

outline.heading: Searching for the right words
outline.gist: Apology or a plea for forgiveness seemed too little to express his remorse.

outline.heading: There is no god but You
outline.gist: His words declare Allah's oneness and perfection and confess wrongdoing; the Prophet said any servant who says them in hardship is given ease.

outline.heading: Darkness upon darkness
outline.gist: It is an apology without detail: You are right and I was wrong; in the darkness of the whale, the sea and the night, the words were his light.

outline.heading: Everyone has a belly of the whale
outline.gist: Allah saved him and promises to save believers likewise; we all face isolation and shame, and calling on Him with these words begins the way out.

outline.heading: Owning the mistake
outline.gist: In an unforeseeable situation he blamed no one but himself; turn to Allah in your darkness with that same remorse.

outline.heading: Magnifying the rituals of Allah
outline.gist: Reverence is the basis of the relationship: we use fitting titles for the Prophet, parents and teachers, and the companions would not stare at his face.

outline.heading: A sign of taqwa in the heart
outline.gist: How much you revere Allah's commands and rituals shows whether your heart has taqwa; praise for contentment, repentance in despair, and reverence form the relationship.

outline.heading: Outro

8:43.en: When Allah showed them unto thee (O Muhammad) in thy dream as few in number, and if He had shown them to thee as many, ye (Muslims) would have faltered and would have quarrelled over the affair. But Allah saved (you). Lo! He knoweth what is in the breasts (of men)

8:44.ar: وَإِذۡ يُرِيكُمُوهُمۡ إِذِ ٱلۡتَقَيۡتُمۡ فِيٓ أَعۡيُنِكُمۡ قَلِيلࣰ ا وَيُقَلِّلُكُمۡ فِيٓ أَعۡيُنِهِمۡ لِيَقۡضِيَ ٱللَّهُ أَمۡرࣰ ا كَانَ مَفۡعُولࣰ اۗ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
8:44.en: And when He made you (Muslims), when ye met (them), see them with your eyes as few, and lessened you in their eyes, (it was) that Allah might conclude a thing that must be done. Unto Allah all things are brought back

rfhXS8QOWYs.title: Ramadan Reminders 1446: Part 2, Badr and Doing What Is Right
rfhXS8QOWYs.one_line: At mid-Ramadan, push through the fatigue, and learn from Badr that open oppression must be answered and truth outweighs every interest.
rfhXS8QOWYs.summary: On the fourteenth of Ramadan, the sheikh reminds listeners that half the month remains and even a sincere final minute can outweigh what others gained all month, so this is the time for repentance and hard questions about one's relationship with Allah. Ramadan is a marathon; the nafs waits until you are tired, then argues you out of Fajr and taraweeh, but growth lies in the last push, so renew your intention. Having worked on less food for two weeks, you have proven you can do more with less, which shows how far needs differ from wants. Ramadan, though, is about what is right. That leads to Badr on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, in the first Ramadan Muslims ever fasted. Comfortable in Medina, some companions resisted going after the caravan carrying their stolen wealth, but the issue was haqq, not money. Openly seized rights, as in Palestine, are not yours to forgive; take them back, then forgive on your own terms. Al-Anfal recounts the reluctance, the promise of one of two outcomes and how each army saw the other as small. In the second khutbah he praises the discipline of the 314, tells of the two boys who killed Abu Jahl, and notes that Abu Jahl died more committed to falsehood than many Muslims are to truth.

outline.heading: Opening
Half the month is left
outline.gist: Tonight marks the middle of Ramadan. Its baraka is such that one sincere final minute can bring what others missed all month, so fourteen wasted days still leave fifteen.

outline.heading: The month of repentance: ask the hard questions
outline.gist: A scholar he cites knew of no repentance reaching its full potential outside Ramadan. Ask yourself how you are doing with Allah, how far down the path you are, and how closely you follow the Prophet.

outline.heading: Never lose hope, even with a day left
outline.gist: If you dislike the answers, that is good news: Allah accepts repentance now and gives the inner strength to turn things around. Even on the last Friday, with a day or two left, effort can achieve what others did not.

outline.heading: It costs only a little more heart
outline.gist: Paradise is open, Hell closed, and Allah calls the lost back to Him. It takes only contemplation, sincerity, standing a little longer and a prostration with more heart in it.

outline.heading: The blessing of all blessings
outline.gist: Once you find it you will never give it up; all the world's riches do not equal it. If you have not found it, keep knocking. Ramadan is a marathon, and Allah looks for grit.

outline.heading: The nafs negotiates when you are tired
outline.gist: Dehydrated and tired mid-month, you start bargaining over Fajr at the masjid and skipping taraweeh because it is only sunnah. The ego fights unfairly, waiting until you are weak.

outline.heading: Growth is in the last push
outline.gist: When you cannot go further but go one more mile, you find your real strength and find Allah. If it were easy everyone would do it; what you ask for is expensive.

outline.heading: Resurface your intention
outline.gist: Allah's commodity is Paradise. Dig the intention you began with out from under the clutter of fatigue, hunger and busyness; you have not reached your goal yet.

outline.heading: The fatigue fades, the regret stays
outline.gist: Ramadan is a few days and will end (2:184). Two days of rest erase the tiredness; what remains is either reward or regret at not having applied yourself.

outline.heading: Not can you, but will you do more with less
outline.gist: Nobody looked forward to work without coffee or school without lunch, yet after fourteen days it is normal. You proved you can do the same job with less sustenance.

outline.heading: What you need versus what you want
outline.gist: When food returns, productivity should rise 20 to 30 percent. Allah shows you need far less than you think; the ego wants everything for itself, and its greed has no end.

outline.heading: Ramadan is about what is right
outline.gist: Ramadan is about neither wants nor needs but what is right. That leads to Badr: 17 Ramadan 2 AH, 1444 lunar years ago, in the first Ramadan Muslims ever fasted.

outline.heading: Go take back what they stole
outline.gist: Desert Arabs had no habit of fasting, yet seventeen days in, the Prophet called them out to Abu Sufyan's caravan carrying their openly stolen wealth. He will teach Badr every Ramadan.

outline.heading: Comfortable believers who disliked the pursuit (8:5)
outline.gist: Two years after the Hijra they were settled, at peace, with the Prophet teaching among them, and had forgotten the stolen wealth. Why poke the bear, they asked, when you taught us wealth does not matter?

outline.heading: Rights openly taken are not yours to forgive
outline.gist: Not daily slights but rights seized openly and never acknowledged, as in Palestine. Forgiving that is weakness and even sinful; take back what is yours, then give it back on your terms, not the oppressor's.

outline.heading: Arguing about the truth after it was clear (8:6)
outline.gist: A Muslim's integrity does not let him give up his right. Some believers argued, frightened, as if being marched to their graves.

outline.heading: Truth outweighs every interest
outline.gist: You do not argue with the right thing; you do it. Truth is the heaviest weight in any decision, above your own or your family's interest. Allah promised one of two outcomes (8:7).

outline.heading: Allah willed the truth established
outline.gist: Most hoped for the caravan, but Allah wanted truth established and falsehood exposed, using the word truth six times in a few verses. The 314 set out, the caravan slipped toward the coast, and Quraysh marched a thousand men.

outline.heading: Three hundred horsemen against two
outline.gist: At Badr a small band stood with the Prophet against a power no one had beaten in decades; Quraysh had more cavalry than the Muslims had soldiers.

outline.heading: The Prophet's dream: they seemed few (8:43-44)
outline.gist: Expecting a slaughter, the companions were afraid until the Prophet told them he had seen the enemy as few. Facing off, the Muslims saw Quraysh as fewer than they were and grew calm.

outline.heading: The day of distinction
outline.gist: Quraysh also saw the Muslims as few and dropped their guard. Allah decreed a day separating truth from falsehood that would never be forgotten; fasting, they won the victory without which most in the room would not be Muslim.

outline.heading: Interlude
Ramadan teaches discipline
outline.gist: The 314 had the inner discipline to march while fasting against an enemy they could not imagine beating. An ummah without self-discipline goes nowhere; each person must hold himself, not others, in check.

outline.heading: Two boys looking for Abu Jahl
outline.gist: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, worried by the odds, felt a tug on each side: two young men asking which one was Abu Jahl, one sent by his mother, the other because he had abused the Prophet. They ran in like arrows and brought him down.

outline.heading: Ibn Mas'ud on Abu Jahl's chest
outline.gist: Both boys claimed the killing blow and the Prophet credited both. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, a small man, then stood on the dying Abu Jahl's chest, and Abu Jahl mocked him as a little shepherd.

outline.heading: Who won today? A man who knew the truth
outline.gist: Dying, Abu Jahl asked who had won, still committed to his cause. He had admitted that Muhammad was truthful but refused to follow him because his clan had no prophet to match.

outline.heading: More committed to falsehood than we are to truth
outline.gist: It is close to pathetic that a man who knew he was wrong was more committed than Muslims who stand for the rights of the oppressed. Ramadan reminds us to put food and distraction aside for what is right.

outline.heading: Outro
